column3: String art. A ring of nails (bright pixel dots) around the panel and one continuous white thread wound nail to nail: the numerals emerge as envelopes of straight chords, curves made only of straight lines, with the dense overlaps glowing brightest. Design a string-art numeral set where each digit is a family of chords whose envelope draws the stroke. Always alive: the thread is being wound right now, one chord travels at a time, the last few strands vibrate like plucked strings. Minute turn: the old digit's thread is unwound backwards nail by nail and the spool rewinds the new figure. Hour: the whole board unwinds into one sweeping cardioid and rewinds.

Airport security X-ray. Bags glide along a conveyor through the scanner tunnel. Inside the tunnel the screen shows the X-ray view: each suitcase's contents (keys, a rubber duck, scissors, a hair dryer, a phone, cables) are drawn in outline and dithered density, and the objects inside are arranged so that their silhouettes ARE the numerals. The belt is always moving slowly, the scanner beam sweeps. Minute turn: the bag holding the old digit rolls out, the next bag rolls in with its contents packed as the new digit, revealed by the beam as it enters. Hour: an alarm, the bag is opened and the contents spill and repack as the new hour.

Sailor's rope work in real 3D: each numeral is a thick braided rope tied into the shape of the digit, a round tube with lay (twist stripes), shading from a light, real over/under crossings with occlusion. The ropes sway slightly as if hanging on a ship's board, the camera eases around. Minute turn: the old knot slips loose, the rope end pulls through and untwists, then is tied, looped, tucked and cinched into the new numeral (you can follow the end). Hour: all four ropes are hauled up on a block and tackle and re-tied in a grand monkey's fist flourish.

A Galton board (bean machine). Balls pour from a hopper through a triangle of pegs and pile into narrow bins at the bottom; the piles are shaped so their columns of balls form the numerals (the bins are slotted so the profile of stacked balls spells digits). Balls always trickle, bouncing off pins with real physics. Minute turn: a gate opens under the changing digit's bins, the balls drain out with a rushing pour, and the new digit fills ball by ball from the hopper. Hour: the board flips over like an hourglass and every ball rains through the pegs. Make the balls round and shaded, never speckle.

A paper fortune teller (cootie catcher) in real 3D. Folded paper with four pointed pockets, opened and closed by unseen fingers in a rhythmic pinch (in-out, side-side), shaded faces and creases, perspective. The numbers are written inside the flaps: each open reveals a pair of inner faces where the hour and minute are inked in hand-lettered numerals. Always alive: the pinching rhythm, a slight wobble. Minute turn: the fortune teller is counted out (open-close, open-close) and a flap is lifted to reveal the new number. Hour: it unfolds fully flat into the square, refolds, and the hour is on the outside.

A wooden tilt maze (Labyrinth game) in 3D. The board is seen in perspective, tilting smoothly on its two knobs; its raised walls form the numerals (the digit shapes are the maze walls, lit with shaded wall tops and shadows), and a polished steel ball rolls through the corridors with real rolling physics, rattling off walls, a specular highlight. Always alive: the board sways and the ball keeps rolling. Minute turn: the walls of the old digit sink into the board, the ball falls into a hole and returns, and the new walls rise. Hour: the board tilts steeply, the ball races the whole maze.

Claymation. The numerals are fat plasticine sausages rolled by hand, with fingerprints and soft rounded shading, squashed and wobbling in a stop-motion style (12 fps 'boiling' outline jitter is part of the look but the motion stays smooth). A thumb pushes into a digit and it squishes. Minute turn: a pair of hands rolls the old numeral into a ball, kneads it, rolls a snake and bends it into the new one, pinching the ends. Hour: a big lump is pounded flat and a cookie cutter stamps the new hour.

Spinning tops in 3D. Each digit is painted on the disc of a spinning top (or the top's body is a lathe shape whose painted bands form the numeral when it spins), seen from a low angle on a table: they spin fast, precess and nutate, wander and lightly bump one another, shadows beneath. Readable thanks to the painted face on top that stays upright in projection. Minute turn: the old top slows, wobbles wider and wider and falls over, rolling away, and a new one is launched with a string pull, landing and stabilising. Hour: a big top with all four, a wild spinning duel.
